introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2, subject code 0575. Time allowed: two and a half hours.

Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three.

Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory to all candidates, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions; if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions).

All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

Chaque question de B et C vaut 17 points imprimes (egalite annoncee par le sujet).
Q14 : points imprimes (i) 3 + 2 + 3 = 8, (ii) 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 = 17, conformes. Q14(i)(b) imprime « p(A'U B) » : lu comme P(A' union B) ; Q14(i)(c) « p(A / B) » lu comme P(A | B).

Q14(ii) : « if he treks is 1/5 » : lu comme P(early | trek) = 1/5. Le (c) demande « early given that he uses a bicycle », qui vaut directement la probabilite donnee 1/3 (question triviale telle qu'imprimee ; pas de lecture inversee supposee).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Two events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A)=\dfrac14$, $P(B)=\dfrac12$, $P(A\cup B)=\dfrac23$.

(a) Find $P(A\cap B)$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Addition rule: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$.

$$
\frac23=\frac14+\frac12-P(A\cap B)\ \Rightarrow\ P(A\cap B)=\frac34-\frac23=\frac{9-8}{12}=\frac1{12}
$$

**$P(A\cap B)=\dfrac1{12}$.**
themes: probability of unions and intersections of events

questions.corrige_markdown:
The complement of $A'\cup B$ is $A\cap B'$, so $P(A'\cup B)=1-P(A\cap B')$.

$P(A\cap B')=P(A)-P(A\cap B)=\dfrac14-\dfrac1{12}=\dfrac{2}{12}=\dfrac16$.

$$
P(A'\cup B)=1-\frac16=\frac56
$$

Check: $P(A')+P(B)-P(A'\cap B)=\dfrac34+\dfrac12-\left(\dfrac12-\dfrac1{12}\right)=\dfrac{9+6-5}{12}=\dfrac{10}{12}=\dfrac56$.

**$P(A'\cup B)=\dfrac56$.**
themes: probability of unions and intersections of events

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Dion goes to school either by trekking or by a bicycle. The probability that Dion gets early to school if he uses a bicycle is $\dfrac13$ and if he treks is $\dfrac15$. Given that the probability that Dion uses a bicycle to school is $\dfrac12$.

Find the probability that on one particular day,

(a) Dion gets early to school. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $B$ = "uses a bicycle", $T$ = "treks", $E$ = "gets early". Then $P(B)=\dfrac12$, $P(T)=\dfrac12$, $P(E\mid B)=\dfrac13$, $P(E\mid T)=\dfrac15$.

Tree diagram (or total probability):

$$
P(E)=P(B)P(E\mid B)+P(T)P(E\mid T)=\frac12\times\frac13+\frac12\times\frac15=\frac16+\frac1{10}=\frac{5+3}{30}=\frac{4}{15}
$$

**$P(\text{early})=\dfrac4{15}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Dion gets to school late. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Late is the complement of early:

$$
P(\text{late})=1-P(E)=1-\frac4{15}=\frac{11}{15}
$$

Check with the tree: $\dfrac12\times\dfrac23+\dfrac12\times\dfrac45=\dfrac13+\dfrac25=\dfrac{5+6}{15}=\dfrac{11}{15}$.

**$P(\text{late})=\dfrac{11}{15}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Dion gets early to school given that he uses a bicycle. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
This is the conditional probability $P(E\mid B)$, which is given in the question:

$$
P(E\mid B)=\frac{P(E\cap B)}{P(B)}=\frac{\frac12\times\frac13}{\frac12}=\frac13
$$

**$P(\text{early}\mid\text{bicycle})=\dfrac13$.**
